title: Servicing Policy Manual: Payment Extensions on the Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract
content:
**Servicing Policy Manual — extensions, Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract.**

## Clauses in force

1. **Status.** An extension can be granted only while the contract status is active.
2. **Counts.** The contract must show installments satisfied of at least the tier's minimum for an extension, days past due of no more than the tier's maximum, and installments deferred over the life of the contract plus the installments requested no greater than the tier's lifetime maximum.
3. **Blackout.** No extension is granted when the remaining installments (the term in months plus the installments deferred over the life of the contract, less the installments satisfied) are the tier's blackout figure or fewer.
4. **Relationship.** No extension is granted while any other Kestrel contract of the customer is repossession assigned, repossessed, deficiency or charged off, or any Kestrel lease of the customer is repossessed or charged off.
5. **Interval.** An extension may take effect no earlier than the tier's interval in calendar months after the previous extension took effect. The interval is counted in calendar months from the last extension date to the same day number of the later month, falling back to that month's last day when the day does not exist; a contract never extended has no interval to wait.
6. **Per request.** One request may defer no more than the tier's maximum installments per request, always starting with the installment due on the next due date.
7. **Agreement.** The agent sends the extension agreement for signature, and it expires if not completed within the tier's agreement return period in calendar days. The extension takes effect only after the customer has completed the signed extension agreement for this contract.
8. **Effect.** On the effective date the next due date and the maturity date each move later by one month per deferred installment, the installments deferred over the life of the contract increase by the number deferred and the last extension date is set; simple interest keeps accruing on principal throughout, so the final installment absorbs the extra interest. Late charges already assessed remain due, and no late charge is assessed on a deferred installment.

## Retired clauses

> "Before the extension is granted, a good-faith payment of at least the tier's good-faith percentage of the monthly payment must have posted since the most recent installment due date; a tier whose percentage is 0 requires none."

> "The extension fee is the tier's extension fee where the contract records that an extension fee is permitted, and 0.00 where it does not; the fee is booked to fees due."

Both clauses are **no longer in force** as the handling basis; they have been superseded by the company's current extension basis.

## The interval as a time test

*Boundary cases (hypothetical, 12-month interval):* after an extension that took effect on 10 June of one year, the next may take effect on 10 June of the following year but not on 9 June; a contract never extended has no interval to wait.

## Counting, illustrated

*Hypothetical:* a 60-month contract with 1 installment deferred over its life and 50 installments satisfied has 11 remaining installments; with a blackout figure of 6 it is outside the blackout. On a tier whose lifetime maximum is 3, the same contract may request up to 2 more installments (1 already deferred plus 2 requested is 3, not greater than 3), subject to the per-request maximum.

superseded_clauses: Before the extension is granted, a good-faith payment of at least extension_good_faith_pct percent of monthly_payment must have posted since the most recent installment due date; a tier whose percentage is 0 requires none.
The extension fee is extension_fee for the tier where the contract records extension_fee_permitted as true, and 0.00 where it is false; the fee is booked to fees due.
